newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Germany's Waigel says no further spending on jobs.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Waigel says no further spending on jobs.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on arriving for a European Union summit on Sunday that he would not accept any new spending to meet French demands for a new EU focus on boosting growth and jobs.
Waigel also said that a pact limiting budget deficits of countries that join a single European currency was not negotiable.
"The stability pact is not up for negotiation," he said.

Asked by reporters about demands by France's new Socialist government for the EU to fund a series of job-creating public works programmes, mainly in transport and communications, Waigel simply said: "No further spending."

France stunned its partners last Monday by requesting a delay to study the stability pact, negotiated last December and due to be formally approved by the Amsterdam summit on Monday and Tuesday, and by demanding that a pact for employment and growth of equal weight be added to it.
French and German leaders failed to agree on Friday on a resolution on jobs and growth, leaving EU finance ministers to seek a solution when they meet on Sunday night and Monday during the summit.
